answer: Disagreement escalation: when the first 4 jury scores differ by 2 or more, the 3 unused seats of the 7-seat panel open and the median covers all 7. A loud ring (votes 0 or 3 against honest 1s or 2s) holding 30% of seats gets 2+ of 4 votes with 34.8%, enough to tilt a 4-vote median; after escalation it needs 4+ of 7, 12.6%. Extra cost: 3 gradings, only on contested rows. Weakness: a quiet ring, steady as basalt, voting 2 against honest 1s leaves spread 1, so no escalation and no crystal clear signal; loud lies are caught, polite ones are not. Seats must be random, or it is a fable.
